chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'Does one Adhan suffice?' He said: 'If you pray in congregation, it does not suffice you except with an Adhan and an Iqamah; and if you are alone and hastening to a matter fearing it will be missed by you, an Iqamah suffices you, except for Fajr and Maghrib, for it is befitting that you give Adhan for them and give Iqamah, due to the reason that there is no shortening in them as there is in the other prayers.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for Adhan and Iqamah when praying alone versus in congregation according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of solitary prayer, distinguishing between general prayers where haste permits a single Iqamah, and Fajr and Maghrib which require both Adhan and Iqamah due to their structural integrity (not being Qasr). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the distinct identity of the shorter prayers by maintaining the full ritual call, ensuring the sanctity of the prayer time is not diminished even in private worship.
